chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from Hamdan al-Qalanisi, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The prisoner's food is upon the one who captured him as a right upon him, and even if he is an infidel who will be killed the next day, it is befitting for him to be kind to him, feed him, and give him drink.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on feeding a prisoner of war in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the juristic principle that feeding the prisoner is a right (haqq) incumbent upon the captor, emphasizing that this obligation persists even for those destined for execution. It underscores the Shia emphasis on humane treatment and mercy (ra'ufah) towards captives, ensuring their sustenance is provided regardless of their faith or ultimate fate.
